messages:
alice.k: Heads-up — customer 'AcmePayments' opened an escalation: streaming responses have p99 TTFB ~600-900ms over the last 24h, but non-streaming (sync) total latency is stable. They see first chunk delayed, then steady streaming. request-id: rwd-7f3b2

ben.s: ack. any correlation with model or region?

alice.k: Model: gpt-medium-q4f, region: us-west-2, traffic ~50rps. Spike aligns with our autoscaler events earlier today but not perfectly. I captured a couple curl traces and runtime logs.

support-joe: can you paste repro steps / curl? I can run against their tenant.

alice.k: repro (streaming):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-rw-tenant: acme" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-q4f","prompt":"short test","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | ts  # expect first chunk ~<100ms
```
repro (sync):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-rw-tenant: acme" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-q4f","prompt":"short test","stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate  # total latency ~120ms consistently
```

maya: thanks. i ran the streaming curl from us-west-2 and saw first event after ~720ms, then chunks every ~30ms. non-stream finished in 140ms.

eng-runtime-bot: trace rwd-7f3b2: route=dedicated-usw2 runtime=batcher-3 flush_window_ms=200 coalesce=true kvcache_hit=0

ben.s: logs show our runtime coalescing/flush_window kicking in. flush_window_ms=200 but that wouldn't explain 700ms TTFB by itself. any front-proxy buffering?

ops-liz: nginx/proxy config for that customer route has proxy_buffering on for SSE endpoints historically (we added for misc edge issues). NGINX doc: proxy_buffering can delay first byte until buffer fills or upstream signals.

alice.k: good catch. acme uses our dedicated edge proxy pool with default proxy_buffering=yes for compatibility. If proxy buffers until 8k or a timeout, small first chunk gets delayed.

support-joe: quick test — set header X-Accel-Buffering: no from runtime to bypass. can we enable a tenant-level override?

eng-runtime-bot: scheduled patch: add immediate header injection for streaming responses when tenant flag streaming_no_buffer=true. rollout candidate to canary.

ben.s: other possibilities: our runtime batcher holding request waiting for KV-cache warmup or for bigger batch. trace shows batcher-3 waited ~480ms before flush trigger; why? maybe backpressure from downsteam or tokenization delay?

maya: i pulled kernel metrics: gpu utilization stable, model latency per-token low. but request queue depth spiked around autoscaler ramp — some requests landed on newly provisioned workers which do cold init of model shards (cold-start can add ~300-500ms). combination of cold-start + proxy buffering = ~800ms.

alice.k: so root cause likely multi-factor: cold-starts during autoscale + proxy buffering + an aggressive coalescing heuristic.

support-joe: immediate mitigations for customer: 1) enable non-streaming fallback (they accept slightly higher total latency but need reliable TTFB), 2) enable streaming_no_buffer tenant flag (bypasses proxy buffering), 3) pin to warm pool (dedicated reserved capacity). Which is easiest?

ops-liz: streaming_no_buffer is quickest — flip tenant flag, rollback if we see downstream regressions. non-streaming fallback is config change client-side. pinning to warm pool requires contract change.

ben.s: medium-term: change runtime coalescer to short-circuit when models are cold-warming or when payload < X bytes; also add explicit header injection to tell proxies not to buffer for text/event-stream + SSE endpoints. add metric: first_chunk_delay_ms tagged by proxy and worker_init.

alice.k: i'm going to patch support ticket with those options and proposed timeline. If customer wants immediate action, i'll toggle streaming_no_buffer and run a canary in their region.

maya: repro note: to simulate, hit API with many small requests while triggering autoscale (scale down then burst) — you'll see TTFB increases on newly spun workers. steps:
1) ensure pool idle (scale to 0 reserved or reduce to min)
2) send 40 concurrent streaming requests
3) observe first_chunk_delay_ms in traces; compare against same test with header X-Accel-Buffering: no

eng-runtime-bot: dashboard created: /dash/first_chunk_delay?tenant=acme&region=us-west-2, alert rule candidate p99>500ms -> paging on-call.

ops-liz: rolling tenant flag now to canary (acme routing) — monitoring windows 15m.

support-joe: customer notified of canary and temporary mitigation path. will update after 15m. :thumbsup:

alice.k: followups: (a) eng-runtime to add header injection + metric (owner: ben.s), (b) eng-sre to audit proxy buffering config (owner: ops-liz), (c) support to document tenant-level flags and recommended mitigations (owner: alice.k).

ben.s: starting PR for header injection and short-circuit for small payloads. linking trace rwd-7f3b2 in PR.

ops-liz: canary shows first_chunk p99 dropped from ~820ms -> ~120ms with streaming_no_buffer enabled for acme. no regressions observed in downstream throughput during 30m check.

support-joe: closing escalation after customer confirms recovery. will add notes to KB: "Streaming TTFB spikes during scale events — quick mitigations".

alice.k: thanks team. tagging follow-up meeting tomorrow 9am PT to discuss long-term coalescer heuristics. :calendar:

maya: leaving traces and the curl snippets in the ticket.

eng-runtime-bot: incident closed (provisional) — monitor for 24h.
